label: input token q during copy phase (and at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for the letter q as input, gated by phase. Fires on every copy-phase step whose input is q (i.e. the model is fed back its own q output), at ~0.65-1.1 activation; 94% of activation mass is in the copy phase. Also fires weakly (~0.22) when q is the very first original token (t=0), and occasionally at t=1. Does NOT fire on q elsewhere in the original phase (t>=2), nor on the delimiter, nor on other tokens (tiny leakage on b). Strongest values occur on a copy-phase q, especially the first of a run of repeated q inputs; magnitude is otherwise roughly flat across position and L.

issues: The test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.954, F1 0.976, mass recall 0.992. There were 0 false positives on test.

The misses are 5180 test steps but hold only 0.8% of the activation mass. They are all in the lowest activation quartile (quartile coverage is 0.82 for the bottom quartile and 1.0 for the others). Most are weak firings (about 0.10-0.13) on q at t=1. A predicate for q at t=1 has precision 0.20 and mass recall 0.005, so it is too weak and noisy to add. The rest is scattered weak firing on tokens next to a copy-phase q.

The secondary claims check out. Phase share is 94.5% copy and 0% delimiter. The rate is flat at about 3.3-3.5% for every recall index. q in the original phase at t>=2 has precision 0.003. b in the copy phase has precision 0.01, which is minor leakage as stated. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
